# Native Waters — full reference

> Sourced reference for the native freshwater fishes of five Indian river systems (Ganga, Brahmaputra, Cauvery, Krishna, Godavari), with an illustrative underwater experience.

Data is derived from cited publications; see the citations on each page and in the Sources section below. Species names follow the cited sources, and basin-native status is only claimed where the cited evidence supports it.

## Rivers

### Ganga

Riverine germplasm connects freshwater biodiversity with restoration. ICAR-CIFRI documents indigenous carps used in its Ganga breeding and ranching programme.

Scope: Ganga river system; no reach-specific occurrence inferred.
Species records: 2

- Rohu (Labeo rohita): status native; basin endemic: no
- Calbasu (Labeo calbasu): status native; basin endemic: no

### Brahmaputra

The upper drainage supports small freshwater fishes as well as the life of the main river. Catalog distribution records provide a starting point without implying that every tributary shares the same fauna.

Scope: Upper Brahmaputra drainage in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh; no precise collection localities published here.
Species records: 1

- Badis blosyrus (Badis blosyrus): status native; basin endemic: no

### Cauvery

A sanctuary survey documents basin-endemic fishes alongside introduced species. Being native to India does not establish native status in the Cauvery.

Scope: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka; survey observations from 2015–2019.
Species records: 8

- Hump-backed mahseer (Tor remadevii): status native; basin endemic: yes
- Arulius barb (Dawkinsia arulius): status native; basin endemic: yes
- Labeo kontius (Labeo kontius): status native; basin endemic: yes
- Hemibagrus punctatus (Hemibagrus punctatus): status native; basin endemic: yes
- Dawkinsia rubrotinctus (Dawkinsia rubrotinctus): status native; basin endemic: yes
- Hypselobarbus dubius (Hypselobarbus dubius): status native; basin endemic: yes
- Hypselobarbus micropogon (Hypselobarbus micropogon): status native; basin endemic: yes
- Kantaka brevidorsalis (Kantaka brevidorsalis): status native; basin endemic: yes

### Krishna

Catfish surveys reveal diversity that can be overlooked in familiar river landscapes. This reference covers a studied Maharashtra stretch, rather than the entire basin.

Scope: Krishna River, Sangli region, Maharashtra; survey from June 2009 to July 2012.
Species records: 1

- Glyptothorax poonaensis (Glyptothorax poonaensis): status native; basin endemic: no

### Godavari

Small tributary streams contribute to basin diversity. A published Blue perch record comes from two sub-basins and does not establish presence throughout the main river.

Scope: Manjeera and Wardha sub-basin streams in Telangana.
Species records: 1

- Blue perch (Badis badis): status uncertain; basin endemic: no

## Conservation status

6 of 13 recorded species are listed in an IUCN threatened category. Categories come from FishBase's mirror of the IUCN Red List (version 2025-2). Not Evaluated means unassessed, not safe.

- Rohu (Labeo rohita): Least Concern (LC)
- Calbasu (Labeo calbasu): Least Concern (LC)
- Hump-backed mahseer (Tor remadevii): Critically Endangered (CR)
- Arulius barb (Dawkinsia arulius): Endangered (EN)
- Labeo kontius (Labeo kontius): Least Concern (LC)
- Hemibagrus punctatus (Hemibagrus punctatus): Critically Endangered (CR)
- Glyptothorax poonaensis (Glyptothorax poonaensis): Endangered (EN)
- Blue perch (Badis badis): Least Concern (LC)
- Badis blosyrus (Badis blosyrus): Least Concern (LC)
- Dawkinsia rubrotinctus (Dawkinsia rubrotinctus): Not Evaluated (NE)
- Hypselobarbus dubius (Hypselobarbus dubius): Endangered (EN)
- Hypselobarbus micropogon (Hypselobarbus micropogon): Endangered (EN)
- Kantaka brevidorsalis (Kantaka brevidorsalis): Least Concern (LC)

## Species

### Rohu (Labeo rohita)

Aliases: none

An indigenous Gangetic carp represented in ICAR-CIFRI’s riverine germplasm programme.

IUCN Red List: Least Concern (LC); assessed: 2010-03-20; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 200 cm TL; maximum published weight: 45 kg.

Environment: Freshwater; brackish; benthopelagic; potamodromous

Distribution: Asia: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Nepal.

- River: Ganga
  - Status: native
  - Basin endemic: no
  - Record area: Ganga river system
  - Evidence period: Programme reports include 2017–2024
  - Note: The source supports indigenous status in the Ganga; it does not support assigning Rohu as native to every Indian river.
  - Citations: ICAR-CIFRI — Seed production and Gangetic riverine germplasm

### Calbasu (Labeo calbasu)

Aliases: none

One of four commercially significant carps selected for the Ganga germplasm programme.

IUCN Red List: Least Concern (LC); assessed: 2010-03-21; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 90 cm TL; maximum published weight: not stated.

Environment: Freshwater; brackish; demersal; potamodromous

Distribution: Asia: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand and south-western China; reported as introduced to China.

- River: Ganga
  - Status: native
  - Basin endemic: no
  - Record area: Ganga river system
  - Evidence period: Programme reports include 2017–2024
  - Note: River ranching is a conservation intervention, not evidence that the species naturally occurs in every reach.
  - Citations: ICAR-CIFRI — Seed production and Gangetic riverine germplasm

### Hump-backed mahseer (Tor remadevii)

Aliases: orange-finned mahseer, Tor remadeviae

The survey identifies the hump-backed mahseer and distinguishes it from unresolved mahseer morphotypes.

IUCN Red List: Critically Endangered (CR); assessed: 2018-04-19; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 175 cm FL; maximum published weight: 54 kg.

Environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic

Distribution: Asia: India.

- River: Cauvery
  - Status: native
  - Basin endemic: yes
  - Record area: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka
  - Evidence period: 2015–2019
  - Note: Reported as endemic to the Cauvery system. No present-day Red List category is inferred from this 2021 paper.
  - Citations: Sreenivasan, Mahesh & Raghavan (2021) — Freshwater fishes of Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary

### Arulius barb (Dawkinsia arulius)

Aliases: none

A barb listed among the Cauvery-system endemics in the sanctuary survey.

IUCN Red List: Endangered (EN); assessed: 2010-06-25; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 12 cm TL; maximum published weight: not stated.

Environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic

Distribution: Asia: Cauvery basin in India.

- River: Cauvery
  - Status: native
  - Basin endemic: yes
  - Record area: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka
  - Evidence period: 2015–2019
  - Note: The basin-endemic designation describes range, not abundance throughout the river.
  - Citations: Sreenivasan, Mahesh & Raghavan (2021) — Freshwater fishes of Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary

### Labeo kontius (Labeo kontius)

Aliases: pigmouth carp

A carp documented among the survey’s Cauvery-system endemics.

IUCN Red List: Least Concern (LC); assessed: 2010-10-03; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 61 cm TL; maximum published weight: not stated.

Environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic; potamodromous

Distribution: Asia: Cauvery river system in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, India.

- River: Cauvery
  - Status: native
  - Basin endemic: yes
  - Record area: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka
  - Evidence period: 2015–2019
  - Note: The record is limited to the study area; the guide does not infer a surveyed underwater scene.
  - Citations: Sreenivasan, Mahesh & Raghavan (2021) — Freshwater fishes of Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary

### Hemibagrus punctatus (Hemibagrus punctatus)

Aliases: Nilgiri mystus

A catfish included among the Cauvery-system endemics.

IUCN Red List: Critically Endangered (CR); assessed: 2010-06-27; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 45 cm TL; maximum published weight: not stated.

Environment: Freshwater; demersal

Distribution: Asia: Cauvery river drainage in southern India.

- River: Cauvery
  - Status: native
  - Basin endemic: yes
  - Record area: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka
  - Evidence period: 2015–2019
  - Note: Locality is intentionally coarse. Historical threat assessments are not displayed as current status.
  - Citations: Sreenivasan, Mahesh & Raghavan (2021) — Freshwater fishes of Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary

### Glyptothorax poonaensis (Glyptothorax poonaensis)

Aliases: none

A sisorid catfish for which the Krishna study reports a range extension.

IUCN Red List: Endangered (EN); assessed: 2010-08-22; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 8 cm TL; maximum published weight: not stated.

Environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic

Distribution: Asia: Mula Mutha river at Pune, Maharashtra, India.

- River: Krishna
  - Status: native
  - Basin endemic: no
  - Record area: Krishna River, Sangli region, Maharashtra
  - Evidence period: June 2009–July 2012
  - Note: The paper describes an endemic Indian fish; this guide does not claim it is endemic to the Krishna basin.
  - Citations: Kumbar & Lad (2014) — Catfish fauna of the Krishna River, Sangli District

### Blue perch (Badis badis)

Aliases: Chameleon fish, Blue badis

A freshwater fish recorded in tributary streams of the Godavari basin.

IUCN Red List: Least Concern (LC); assessed: 2010-03-26; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 7.1 cm TL; maximum published weight: not stated.

Environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic

Distribution: Asia: Ganges River drainage in India, Bangladesh and Nepal, from Himachal Pradesh (Yamuna River) to the estuary; also the Mahanadi drainage and Assam lowlands near the Brahmaputra.

- River: Godavari
  - Status: uncertain
  - Basin endemic: no
  - Record area: Manjeera and Wardha sub-basins, Telangana
  - Evidence period: Published 2019; observation dates not transcribed
  - Note: Occurrence is documented. This record alone does not resolve whether the Godavari populations are native or introduced.
  - Citations: Prasad & Srinivasulu (2019) — New record of Badis badis from the Godavari basin

### Badis blosyrus (Badis blosyrus)

Aliases: none

A valid badid species whose catalog distribution includes the upper Brahmaputra drainage in northeastern India.

IUCN Red List: Least Concern (LC); assessed: 2010-03-26; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 4.2 cm SL; maximum published weight: not stated.

Environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic

Distribution: Asia: India.

- River: Brahmaputra
  - Status: native
  - Basin endemic: no
  - Record area: Upper Brahmaputra drainage, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh
  - Evidence period: Catalog distribution reviewed 2026-10-23; no observation date stated
  - Note: A regional natural-range summary, not evidence of ubiquitous main-channel occurrence. No microhabitat or basin-endemic claim is made.
  - Citations: Eschmeyer’s Catalog of Fishes — Badis blosyrus

### Dawkinsia rubrotinctus (Dawkinsia rubrotinctus)

Aliases: none

Listed among the Cauvery-system endemic freshwater fishes in the sanctuary survey.

IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated (NE); assessed: not assessed; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 8.6 cm SL; maximum published weight: not stated.

Environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic

Distribution: Asia: Cauvery and its tributaries across Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, India.

- River: Cauvery
  - Status: native
  - Basin endemic: yes
  - Record area: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka
  - Evidence period: 2015–2019
  - Note: The cited survey establishes a historical record and reports basin endemism; it does not establish present abundance, a current threat category or a specific microhabitat.
  - Citations: Sreenivasan, Mahesh & Raghavan (2021) — Freshwater fishes of Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary

### Hypselobarbus dubius (Hypselobarbus dubius)

Aliases: Nilgiris barb, cock fish

Listed among the Cauvery-system endemic freshwater fishes in the sanctuary survey.

IUCN Red List: Endangered (EN); assessed: 2010-06-21; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 25 cm TL; maximum published weight: not stated.

Environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic; potamodromous

Distribution: Asia: India.

- River: Cauvery
  - Status: native
  - Basin endemic: yes
  - Record area: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka
  - Evidence period: 2015–2019
  - Note: The cited survey establishes a historical record and reports basin endemism; it does not establish present abundance, a current threat category or a specific microhabitat.
  - Citations: Sreenivasan, Mahesh & Raghavan (2021) — Freshwater fishes of Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary

### Hypselobarbus micropogon (Hypselobarbus micropogon)

Aliases: Korhi barb

Listed among the Cauvery-system endemic freshwater fishes in the sanctuary survey.

IUCN Red List: Endangered (EN); assessed: 2021-03-06; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 90 cm TL; maximum published weight: not stated.

Environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic; potamodromous

Distribution: Asia: headwaters of the Cauvery in the Nilgiris, Wayanad and Karnataka, India.

- River: Cauvery
  - Status: native
  - Basin endemic: yes
  - Record area: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka
  - Evidence period: 2015–2019
  - Note: The cited survey establishes a historical record and reports basin endemism; it does not establish present abundance, a current threat category or a specific microhabitat.
  - Citations: Sreenivasan, Mahesh & Raghavan (2021) — Freshwater fishes of Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary

### Kantaka brevidorsalis (Kantaka brevidorsalis)

Aliases: none

Listed among the Cauvery-system endemic freshwater fishes in the sanctuary survey.

IUCN Red List: Least Concern (LC); assessed: 2010-08-10; list version: 2025-2 (Global).

Maximum recorded length: 15 cm TL; maximum published weight: not stated.

Environment: Freshwater; benthopelagic

Distribution: Asia: endemic to India.

- River: Cauvery
  - Status: native
  - Basin endemic: yes
  - Record area: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka
  - Evidence period: 2015–2019
  - Note: The cited survey establishes a historical record and reports basin endemism; it does not establish present abundance, a current threat category or a specific microhabitat.
  - Citations: Sreenivasan, Mahesh & Raghavan (2021) — Freshwater fishes of Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary
